The core insight emerges from combining Bayesian filtering with conformal inference to ensure both accurate tracking and reliable uncertainty bounds. The state estimation primitive models each object's trajectory through a probabilistic lens, updating beliefs based on sequential observations. This is complemented by conformal predictive inference which provides finite-sample validity guarantees on predictions—critical for safety-sensitive applications. The multi-object tracking pipeline integrates these components into a coherent system that maintains identity over time while adapting to environmental changes. Dualities manifest in how uncertainty propagation in Bayesian estimation aligns with the validity constraints imposed by conformal inference. Failure modes include divergence in belief updates under model misspecification or breakdown in exchangeability assumptions, leading to unreliable confidence intervals.
